fatal_errors: The proposed initially single-phase alloy does not match the as-cast dual-phase FCC+B2 AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA.

The hypothesis invokes conventional grain-boundary segregation and brittle grain-boundary precipitation, whereas the target mechanism is L12 ordering within FCC domains coupled to jagged FCC/B2 phase boundaries.
It misses the non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile response, including maximum embrittlement near 600°C and recovery near 750°C.
It does not reconstruct the operative 550-750°C aging window or the absence of the transition below about 550°C.
No supporting prior evidence is supplied despite the request for it.
explanation: The response is testable in isolation and proposes useful TEM/APT measurements, but it largely restates the conventional-alloy expectation that segregation and brittle grain-boundary phases reduce cohesion. That is the mechanism the controlled comparison needed to distinguish from. The hidden result instead concerns a dual-phase eutectic HEA in which enhanced L12 ordering raises APBE and modulus, restricts cross-slip, and promotes planar slip and dislocation pile-ups; stress concentrations at jagged FCC/B2 phase-boundary tips then initiate instability and cracking. Higher-temperature aging suppresses ordering and creates ductile transition zones, restoring ductility. An aged-versus-unaged comparison at an unspecified intermediate temperature cannot reveal this non-monotonic temperature dependence. Although the proposed absence of segregation or grain-boundary phases could falsify the submitted mechanism, the design lacks the multi-temperature comparison and phase-boundary-resolved observations needed to identify the target mechanism.
